headline: Point at what you want out of the rack
lede: Tidy Bot's dishwasher rack got real slots and a targeting system: tap an item in an open cavity and the bot marks it, walks to the rack, and B pulls out exactly the one you named — plates and apples finally answer to you, not to the queue. On the keyboard, B plus a direction picks the stow furthest that way; and if you say nothing, the old wrong-stow rescue law still rules, byte-for-byte.

notes.text: TIDY BOT aimed retrieve shipped (#2338, PR #2340): stable rack slots as engine state, tap-to-aim with teal brackets, B+direction pulls, wrong-first default untouched — tidycheck 103/103 with a mutant that names three clauses red when aiming dies.

The browser gates earned their keep: a unit-level reading said the wiring was fine, but the real B-key press was clearing its own target before the pad could carry it. Commit buttons must never cancel themselves.
The prod stall (#2335) moved but isn't dead: the alias flipped its entry chunk mid-shift, yet all 51 lazy game chunks still predate the merge. Dashboard eyes still needed.
Slot b's parallel shift landed VIPER PIT destructible props + meter pickups (#2341) — both builder lanes shipped this session.
